facts.statement: Quasipetalichthys haikouensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Quasipetalichthys.
facts.quote: Quasipetalichthys haikouensis is the type and only known species of the extinct petalichthid placoderm, Quasipetalichthys.

facts.statement: Fossils of Quasipetalichthys date to the Middle Devonian Givetian stage in China.
facts.quote: Fossil remains of Quasipetalichthys have been found in the Middle Devonian, Givetian faunal stage of China.

facts.statement: The largest known skull of Quasipetalichthys may have reached approximately 10 cm in length.
facts.quote: The larger of the two skulls may have been around 10 cm in length.

facts.statement: Quasipetalichthys fossils were found alongside antiarch placoderms like Bothriolepis sinensis and Hunanolepis.
facts.quote: Quasipetalichthys is known primarily from two poorly preserved skulls from the Givetian-aged Haikou Formation of Haikou, Kunming, China, where they were found in association with remains of antiarch placoderms such as Bothriolepis sinensis, and Hunanolepis.

facts.statement: Quasipetalichthys is considered a basal member of the Petalichthyidae, though some researchers once called it aberrant.
facts.quote: Quasipetalichthys haikouensis is considered a basal petalichthyid (though in 1978 Denison referred to it as being "aberrant").

facts.statement: Eurycaraspis is placed in the family Quasipetalichthyidae as a sister taxon to Quasipetalichthys.
facts.quote: Whether or not Neopetalichthys is included in the family, Eurycaraspis is placed in Quasipetalichthyidae as a sister taxon toQuasipetalichthys.

facts.statement: Quasipetalichthys fossils are found exclusively in the Haikou Formation, which is exposed in south-central China.
facts.quote: The Haikou Formation, the only known set of rocks that has produced fossils of Quasipetalichthys, appears at the Earth's surface in south-central China.

facts.statement: The presence of Devonian plants alongside placoderm fossils suggests Quasipetalichthys lived in a near-shore or freshwater environment.
facts.quote: These plant remains often occur alongside those of Placoderms such as Bothriolepis which implies a very near-shore or freshwater environment for this geologic formation.

facts.statement: Quasipetalichthys belongs to the class Placodermi.
Quasipetalichthys lived between 387.95 and 372.15 million years ago, spanning the Givetian to Frasnian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Frasnian (387.95 to 372.15 million years ago)
